# CONFORMANCE

The conformance ID register. Every test name ends in its ID; a test whose
ID is not listed here fails `cargo xtask check-model`, and so does an ID
listed here with no scenario and no test (`CM-02`).

The three honesty levels (R2):

| Level | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `some-true` | A fact reproduced from an authority. **Not established here.** |
| `build` | Constructed here and validated against its oracle. Evidence, not a proof. |
| `open` | Measured and reported. **Never asserted.** |

`cargo xtask audit-limits` fails if any code path returns an error the
model does not sanction.

## chaoss

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CC-01` | `build` | The CHAOSS register is valid: every released metric and metrics model is numbered and counted against the release, every model names only declared metrics or its own measures, and every open claim names a declared model |
| `CC-02` | `build` | The CHAOSS catalog declares every metric and metrics model of chaoss/register.json with the content digest of its pinned working-group source |
| `CC-03` | `open` | A released CHAOSS item the projector cannot match to a definition is carried as an open claim, never dropped or guessed |
| `CC-04` | `build` | Every CHAOSS metric and metrics model has a complete ISO/IEC 15939 mapping: each element of its measurement information model is either stated from a CHAOSS template section cited by digest or carried as a typed open claim |
| `CC-05` | `open` | An ISO/IEC 15939 element the CHAOSS templates do not carry, or a definition omits, is an open claim with its reason, never inferred from prose |

## health

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `HL-01` | `build` | Every health assessment's answer is its metrics model's indicator answer: the compiled judge of that model's decision app, applied to the assessment's admitted and refused counts |
| `HL-02` | `build` | Every health assessment's counts are exactly what its evidence rows admit and refuse, plus the members the CHAOSS register carries as open claims; each row is a distinct observable base measure of the indicator, and a row with a computed value has a permitted observation |
| `HL-03` | `build` | The health register is the projection of the CHAOSS, ecosystem and observation registers and the indicator prompts, evaluated as DMN 1.5 first-hit decision tables that answer every example their prompts state, and the Health catalog is its catalog; a register or catalog that differs fails the gate |
| `HL-04` | `build` | Every stakeholder view shows the current health of each metrics model it holds, and the health page, its Markdown twin and the Discord digest carry every indicator's answers, all generated from the health register |
| `HL-05` | `open` | A registered repository the observation corpus never reached, a metrics model with no indicator app, and an observation of a subject outside the ecosystem register are carried as open claims, never assessed by default |

## observations

| ID | Level | Statement |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OB-01` | `build` | The observation register is valid: every observation's admission is what the uor-observation-admission app's first-applicable rules decide on its recorded fields, and every metric value refers to a permitted observation of its own metric, so every value is a function of admitted observations |
| `OB-02` | `build` | The observation corpus is frozen and replayable: every subject is pinned by the commits of its refs, every corpus file is pinned by the sha256 of its bytes, an independent run from the same pins reproduces each file, and the register and its catalog declare the corpus digest |
| `OB-03` | `build` | Every contribution is credited through the uor-contribution-attribution app as W3C PROV-O: a person is credited for their own work, a software agent's work is credited to a person only through a Co-authored-by delegation naming exactly one person, and no name or email enters the corpus |
| `OB-04` | `open` | A released CHAOSS metric the oracle binds no computation to, and a computation whose index, field, query, aggregation or script this corpus and projector cannot evaluate exactly as the oracle defines it, is carried as an open claim, never approximated |
| `OB-05` | `open` | GitHub issues and pull requests enter the corpus only from responses the observations workflow recorded with a token and replayed offline, and the Foundation's Discord only once its read-only bot is installed; until then their observations are open claims |
